_comment: Shared cases for the field-name uniqueness rule, which is implemented TWICE: once in Java
stored) and once in TypeScript (buildOperationRequest.withUniqueFieldNames, which the
confirmation preview uses to show the user those same names before they commit).
Both had their own tests and nothing pinned them to each other, so a change to the suffix
format on one side left the preview promising names the server would not store, with both
suites green (parallel review, A10). Asserted from InventoryOperationRequestBuilderTest and
from buildOperationRequest.test.ts; a change to the rule must be made on both sides or one of
A field is {name, type, targetGlobalId}. type 'link' is the only one disambiguated by its
target; anything else falls back to an ordinal.

cases.description: names that do not collide are left exactly as they are
colliding links are BOTH suffixed by target, so the names stay symmetrical
collision is judged trimmed and case-insensitively, as the backend judges it
a non-link collision has no target to use, so it falls back to an ordinal
two links sharing a name AND a target: the suffixed names collide in turn, so the second takes an ordinal on top
a link colliding with a non-link: only the link gets a target suffix
